issueTitle: desktop,web:feat: surface multi-CLI runtime support — onboarding + installed-CLI detection

plan.summary: Make Skipper's four agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, Gemini) discoverable and self-diagnosing: upgrade the main-process installed-CLI probe to a cached `<cli> --version` spawn that can be refreshed when Settings opens, expose it over the existing `skipper:runtimes:status` IPC, stop filtering un-installed CLIs out of the runtime selects in favour of installed / not-found badges plus an install hint, and add an onboarding card that presents all four CLIs with Claude Code preselected and a link to the Runtimes settings.

ambiguities.detail: Where in onboarding the CLI card lives — a new dedicated step versus a card inside an existing step (the plan silently picks the existing `settings` step)
Whether the onboarding card is purely informational or an actual selection control that writes the chosen runtime to settings ('preselected' implies selectable but is never pinned down)
Cache lifetime/invalidation policy for the probe — TTL, per-session, or only invalidated by the settings-open refresh
Probe timeout and failure semantics: how long to wait on `<cli> --version`, and whether timeout/non-zero exit maps to 'not found' or a distinct unknown/error state
Whether the detected version string is surfaced in the UI or only a boolean installed/not-found
IPC channel name and payload shape, and whether an existing channel (`skipper:runtimes:status`) is extended with a `refresh` argument or a new one added
Install hint text/command for each of the four runtimes — only the Gemini example is given

That the existing selects currently filter out un-installed runtimes and that this filtering must be removed (the issue says 'keep selects un-gated' but never states current filtering behaviour); also whether the existing auto-switch-away-from-missing-runtime effect should be deleted
Whether the web target gets the same treatment as desktop, given probing requires a main process — issue is labelled both desktop and web but only describes a main-process probe
Loading/indeterminate presentation while the probe is in flight (no badge, spinner, or optimistic 'installed')
Badge visual treatment and placement within the option rows, and whether hints show inline per option or once below the select

clarity.rationale: The two 'Done when' bullets are objectively checkable in outline, but the issue leaves the probe's caching/timeout/error semantics, the onboarding card's placement and whether it actually selects a runtime, and badge presentation to the implementer — all of which the plan decided silently, raising no questions.

objections.detail: The probe stays SYNCHRONOUS on the Electron main thread while getting far more expensive. `apps/desktop/src/main.ts:445-447` wires `exec: (cmd) => execSync(cmd, { stdio: "ignore", windowsHide: true })` and `detectRuntimes` (runtimes-ipc.ts:43-50) loops all four binaries in-line. `command -v` is a shell builtin costing ~ms; `<cli> --version` spawns four Node-based CLIs. Step 2 adds a per-call `timeout` of "a few seconds" — worst case that is 4 × timeout of a fully frozen main process (no IPC, no PTY, no window events) on the very path step 9 triggers on every Settings open. The plan never converts the `exec` dep to an async promise-returning spawn, and that conversion is not a detail: it changes `RuntimesIpcDeps`, makes `detectRuntimes` async, changes the handler and rewrites every case in `runtimes-ipc.test.ts`. As specced, opening Settings can hang the app for seconds.

The onboarding "link to the Runtimes settings" cannot work as designed. `OnboardingGate` (apps/web/src/lib/onboarding-gate.tsx:39-45) renders `<OnboardingFlow>` as a sibling ON TOP of `children`, and OnboardingFlow's root is `fixed inset-0 z-[100] bg-black/85` (onboarding.tsx:96). A `Link href="/settings"` inside `SupportedRuntimesCard` routes the app underneath the overlay, but the overlay stays until `onboardingCompleted` is written — the user clicks and sees nothing change. Step 8 gives no dismiss/finish-then-navigate handling, so acceptance criterion 1 ("...and a link to the Runtimes settings") is not actually met.

The issue's second premise is as stale as the first one the plan caught, and the plan missed it: there is no "Runtimes" card in Settings → Orchestration. Grepping `apps/web/src` for `Runtimes` yields only the `noRuntimesInstalled` string; orchestration-section.tsx renders per-role `AgentPairRow`s and a floor note, nothing else. So "the Runtimes settings show per-CLI availability" has no home other than the select option labels, and the onboarding link points at `/settings` with no such section to land on. The plan even describes `supported-runtimes-card.tsx` as "reused by onboarding" but never mounts it in `settings/page.tsx` — mounting it there (near `DefaultAgentSection`) is the one change that would satisfy done-when #2 head-on and give the onboarding link a real target.

The install commands are already in the tree, so `install-hints.ts` creates a second source of truth: `packages/core/src/llm/claude-cli.ts:300` (`npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`), `codex-cli.ts:297` (`@openai/codex`), `copilot-cli.ts:308` (`@github/copilot`), `gemini-cli.ts:397` (`@google/gemini-cli`), each asserted by tests in `packages/core/tests/*-cli-agent.test.ts`. The plan's stated risk ("the npm package names ... are not written anywhere in the repo ... double-check against each vendor's docs") is simply wrong, and independently re-typing them in the web layer means the badge hint and the run-failure message can drift apart. Source them from one shared constant instead of retyping.

Copy that the plan explicitly keeps becomes false. `settings.orchestration.noRuntimesInstalled` reads "No agent CLI found. Install ... and restart Skipper." in all four locales (settings.ts:211/477/743/1009, asserted verbatim in runtime-select.test.ts:77-79) — step 6 keeps it "as an informational line" while step 9's refresh-on-settings-open makes the restart advice wrong. Symmetrically, step 5 claims `missingRuntimes` is "still used for copy", but its only consumer is the `alsoSupports` line in runtime-auth-hint.tsx:24,35 which step 7 deletes; after that both `missingRuntimes` and `settings.llm.alsoSupports` (four locales) are dead. Neither the restart wording nor the dead key/export cleanup appears in any step.

Two existing test harnesses break in ways step 11 does not mention. (a) `runtimes-ipc.test.ts:28-31` derives the probed binary with `cmd.split(" ").pop()`; under `claude --version` that returns `"--version"`, so every probe throws and every availability expectation flips to false — the helper, not just the expected strings, has to change. (b) `runtime-select.test.ts:9` mocks the module as `vi.mock("@/lib/runtime-availability", () => ({ getRuntimeAvailability: vi.fn() }))`; switching RuntimeSelect to `useRuntimeAvailability()` (step 6) makes that factory incomplete and the component read `undefined` as a hook. Same for the new `supported-runtimes-card.test.tsx`, which the plan says to model on that mock.

Step 8 deletes the onboarding preselect effect (onboarding.tsx:46-52) whose comment states its purpose — "onboarding must never dead-end on a missing CLI". After deletion, a fresh user with only Codex installed saves `defaultAgent = { runtime: "claude-cli", model: "sonnet" }` and their first run parks in needs-input, which is exactly the outcome the issue says to avoid ("instead of letting the first run park in needs-input"). The issue's "default (Claude Code) preselected" is about the initial state, not about forbidding a fallback; keeping Claude when it is installed or unknown and switching only when it is provably absent satisfies both readings without the regression.

The install hint is rendered by three different components in one view with no ownership rule: step 6 puts it under RuntimeSelect, step 7 puts it in RuntimeAuthHint, and step 8 puts it in SupportedRuntimesCard — all three sit inside the same onboarding `settings` card (onboarding.tsx:170-195 plus the new card), so a user who picks a missing CLI sees the same `npm install -g …` line three times. In Orchestration, RuntimeSelect returns a fragment, so its new hint line lands directly in AgentPairSelect's layout for each of the per-role rows. Decide one owner for the hint (the card, or the auth-hint block) and keep RuntimeSelect to the option badge.

Swapping `command -v` for `<cli> --version` trades a pure existence check for a behavioural one: the badge now says "not found" for any installed CLI whose `--version` is unsupported, exits nonzero, prompts, or is slower than the new timeout — and the plan keeps the known-locations fallback only on win32, so POSIX has no safety net. A cheap `command -v` first with `--version` only as confirmation (or a fallback to `command -v` when `--version` throws) would keep false negatives off the badge. I did not verify each vendor CLI's `--version` behaviour, so treat this as a question.
